name: GraphVAE
tagline: Variational autoencoder for graphs: GCN encoder pools to a graph-level latent; MLP decoder reconstructs symmetric adjacency probabilities.
diff_from_baseline: Simonovsky & Komodakis, 'GraphVAE: Towards Generation of Small Graphs Using Variational Autoencoders' (ICANN 2018, arXiv:1802.03480). Graph-level VAE with GCN encoder, mean pooling, and MLP decoder over flattened adjacency; classic latent-variable baseline for small-graph generation.

name: GRAN
tagline: Graph Recurrent Attention Network: alternating attention-based node updates and pairwise edge-MLP updates, refined for several iterations.
diff_from_baseline: Liao et al., 'Efficient Graph Generation with Graph Recurrent Attention Networks' (NeurIPS 2019). One-shot generator with iterative attention-based message passing over node-pair edge features; reference attention-based graph generator.

name: DiGress (discrete diffusion)
tagline: Discrete denoising diffusion: edge flips with cosine $\alpha$ schedule, graph-transformer denoiser predicts the clean adjacency at each step.
pseudocode:
1. Sample timestep $t \sim U(0,T)$ and corrupt $A_t = A_0 \oplus B_t$ (XOR flip)
2. Symmetrize $A_t$ and zero its diagonal
3. Graph transformer (with edge-bias attention) reads $A_t$ and time-embed and outputs edge logits + node-existence logits
4. Train with binary cross-entropy on the clean adjacency and node mask
5. Sample: start from random binary $A_T$ then iteratively re-denoise via the predicted $p(A_0\mid A_t)$ down to $A_0$
diff_from_baseline: Vignac et al., 'DiGress: Discrete Denoising Diffusion for Graph Generation' (ICLR 2023). Discrete absorbing/edge-flip diffusion with a graph-transformer denoiser; the canonical discrete-diffusion reference for graph generation.

name: GDSS
tagline: Score-based generative model for graphs via VP-SDE on adjacency entries with denoising score matching and Euler-Maruyama reverse sampling.
pseudocode:
1. Sample $t \in [0.001, 0.999]$ and add VP-SDE noise to $A_0$ (symmetrize $\epsilon$, zero diagonal)
2. Score net $s_\theta(A_t,t)$ runs GCN aggregation + MLP and predicts the score
3. Score-matching loss: minimize $\lVert s_\theta + \epsilon/\sigma_t\rVert^2$ on off-diagonal entries
4. Reverse SDE (Euler-Maruyama): $A \leftarrow A - \tfrac{1}{2}\beta(t)(A + s_\theta)\,dt + \sqrt{\beta(t)\,dt}\,\eta$
5. Threshold final $A$ at zero, symmetrize, derive node mask from row-sums
diff_from_baseline: Jo, Lee & Hwang, 'Score-based Generative Modeling of Graphs via the System of Stochastic Differential Equations' (ICML 2022). VP-SDE on adjacency with denoising score matching; canonical score-based reference for graph generation.

name: MoFlow (flow)
tagline: Normalizing flow over upper-triangular adjacency entries: stack of ActNorm + affine coupling blocks trained by maximum likelihood.
formula: $$\log p(A) = \log \mathcal{N}(z; 0, I) + \sum_k \log\!\left|\det \frac{\partial f_k}{\partial \cdot}\right|, \quad z = (f_K \circ \cdots \circ f_1)(\mathrm{vec}_{\Delta}(A) + \xi),\; \xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.05^2 I)$$
pseudocode:
1. Vectorize the strict upper triangle $\mathrm{vec}_\Delta(A)$ and add $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.05^2)$ dequantization noise
2. Pass through $K$ Glow-style blocks (ActNorm + affine coupling) producing $z$ and $\sum \log|\det J|$
3. Maximize log-likelihood under $\mathcal{N}(0, I)$ prior
4. Side head from $\mathrm{vec}_\Delta(A)$ predicts node-existence (BCE)
5. Sample $z \sim 0.6\cdot\mathcal{N}(0,I)$, invert flow, threshold at zero, scatter back into symmetric $\hat{A}$
diff_from_baseline: Zang & Wang, 'MoFlow: An Invertible Flow Model for Generating Molecular Graphs' (KDD 2020). Normalizing-flow reference adapted here to upper-triangular adjacency entries with Glow-style ActNorm + affine coupling blocks.
